continuity_scope: Fritz Leiber, Jr.'s “Two Sought Adventure” exactly as published in Unknown, vol. 1 no. 6 (August 1939). This is the original magazine witness and uses its original title, not the later title “The Jewels in the Forest,” its collection texts, later revised/expanded collections, later Lankhmar/Nehwon stories, post-Leiber continuations, comics, games, or other adaptations.

work_or_witnesses.edition: Unknown, vol. 1 no. 6, August 1939; published as by Fritz Leiber, Jr.; Internet Archive scan identifier Unknown_v01n06_1939-08_JvH-slpn.
The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction, bibliography/context entry; used to distinguish the August 1939 publication from the later title and collections, not as evidence for plot claims.
Hachette publisher feature; used only for publication-context corroboration.

coverage_rule: Include all named individual protagonists, the named material rival, the named onstage claimant to the Angarngi legacy, and the named deceased architect whose documented trap physically drives the climax: Fafhrd, the Gray Mouser, Lord Rannarsh, Arvlan of Angarngi, and Urgaan of Angarngi. Unnamed peasants, Rannarsh's unnamed retainers, unnamed/collective divinities, the unnamed gray guardian, the House of Angarngi, treasure, magic, and locations remain dimensions or source terms. This pass is complete only for that five-person cohort in this exact 1939 story.
omissions: Every Fafhrd and Gray Mouser work other than the August 1939 “Two Sought Adventure” magazine witness, including the retitled “The Jewels in the Forest” and all collection/revision variants
The remaining Lankhmar/Nehwon sequence, material by Harry Otto Fischer or later writers, and all comics, games, screen works, and other adaptations
Unnamed peasants, the peasant girl, Rannarsh's unnamed henchmen, the unnamed gray guardian/house-beast, and unnamed supernatural powers
Gods, locations, the House of Angarngi, treasure, weapons, prayers, cantrips, and magic, which are terms/dimensions rather than character nodes
uncertainties: The story has a title and publication-history ambiguity: it first appeared as “Two Sought Adventure” in August 1939 and was later retitled “The Jewels in the Forest”; this pass does not conflate the magazine wording with later texts or collection order.

The Internet Archive makes a scan accessible but is not treated as a copyright or public-domain determination. The story remains subject to applicable rights; this pass supplies no extended quotation or legal advice.

Urgaan is a deceased offstage figure. His identity, motives, and acts are mediated by documents and Arvlan's account inside the story; those claims are intentionally qualified rather than treated as independently observed fact.

The 1939 narration labels Fafhrd a barbarian and assigns rural/city contrasts to characters. These are retained only as period, source-specific fictional language and are not mapped to real peoples, classes, cultures, or ethnicities.
evidence_basis: All character, relationship, and source-term claims use the August 1939 Unknown scan and its downloadable full-text transcription, cited by story title and line range. The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction and Hachette provide bibliographic context for the first publication and later variant/sequence history.
